title: Priority-aware queue-depth controller for dedicated pool admission and adaptive shedding
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background: Dedicated pools occasionally experience short bursts of traffic that exceed provisioned throughput. Current admission behavior is coarse: global rate limits and single shared queue per pool leading to head-of-line blocking and brittle tail latencies for premium tenants. We need an admission mechanism that enforces per-tenant and per-route throughput guarantees while enabling graceful degradation for best-effort traffic and avoiding full pool-wide collapse.

Proposal: Implement a Priority-Aware Queue-Depth Controller (PAQDC) at the dedicated ingress routing layer. Key ideas: 1) Per-tenant token buckets for long-term throughput guarantees (tokens refilled by configured throughput SLA); 2) Multi-priority in-memory queues: HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW (configurable), each with adaptive soft/hard queue-depth thresholds; 3) Dynamic shedding: if queue depth for a priority exceeds its soft limit, incoming LOW/MEDIUM requests get rate-limited or enqueued with a short TTL; if hard limit reached or pool under severe overload (based on queue latency and GPU utilization), shed according to configured policies (return 429 or synthetic fallback); 4) Autoscaling integration: signals from the cluster autoscaler (targeted scale-up pending) temporarily relax shedding for high-priority traffic and accelerate token refill for tenants with committed capacity; 5) Fast-fail path for cold-start and model-load-heavy requests (preflight checks); 6) Observability hooks and per-tenant counters for admitted/shed/enqueue/timeout to enable SLA reconciliation and billing adjustments.

Config surface: single YAML blob loaded by routing layer: 
- priorities: [HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW]
- per_priority: {HIGH: {soft_queue: 256, hard_queue: 1024, admission_policy: "enqueue"}, MEDIUM: {soft_queue: 128, hard_queue: 512, admission_policy: "enqueue_or_rate_limit"}, LOW: {soft_queue: 64, hard_queue: 256, admission_policy: "shed"}}
- tenant_buckets: map of tenant -> {rate_tokens_per_sec, burst_tokens}
- scale_inhibit_window_seconds: 60
- tail_latency_trigger_ms: {p95: 300, p99: 800}
- fallback_response: {status: 429, body_template: "service overloaded, try again in Xs"}

Admission outcomes: accept (direct to serving), enqueue (wait in priority queue, with estimated wait returned to client when supported), shed (immediate 429 or materialized fallback). We will support both synchronous clients (429) and async/queued flow with status endpoints.

Metrics and signals: admitted_rate_by_tenant, shed_rate_by_tenant, queue_depth_by_priority, enqueue_latency_p50/p95/p99, token_bucket_fill, pool_utilization, pending_scale_up (bool), overload_incidents. These metrics must feed into console dashboards and automated alerting (SRE guardrails).

Compatibility: Works with existing routing policies (region/tier/model-version). Default behavior preserves current semantics for pools with no tenant SLA config. Migration strategy is opt-in per pool, with a rollout guard to disable PAQDC per pool via config.

Trade-offs and limits: In-memory queues reduce I/O latency but increase memory footprint per-router instance; we limit queue sizes and prefer shedding low-priority traffic under extreme memory pressure. Token-bucket guarantees are soft — committed throughput must map to reserved capacity (Dedicated) to be enforceable without harming non-committed tenants.

Rollout plan: 1) Unit + integration tests (2 weeks); 2) Offline simulation using historical ingress traces (bench harness) to tune soft/hard thresholds (1 week); 3) Canary on non-critical dedicated pool (5% traffic) with detailed telemetry (2 weeks); 4) Expand to 25% and then 100% with staged policy activation and audit logs.

Success criteria: p99 latency for HIGH-priority tenants remains within 1.2x baseline under 2x traffic bursts; shed_rate for HIGH <= 0.5% under target loads; system recovers to baseline within autoscaler target time for scale-up events.

References: design doc (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/PAQDC), perf bench run (https://perf.redwood.ai/runs/paqdctest-2026-02), initial PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/7421).
comments: 2026-02-12 - Initial draft created. Captured goals and first-pass config knobs. Assigned to Daniel Kim for implementation spike.
2026-02-16 - Spike results: in-memory queues with per-priority ring buffer keep p99 enqueue latency < 50ms for nominal loads. Need to cap memory usage; added soft/hard queue limits in config.

2026-02-20 - Architecture review with SRE and Product: agreed on token-bucket for tenant guarantees and that billing teams will own tenant SLA config. Action: add audit log entries for any shed events (PM request).

2026-02-24 - Implementation started: initial router hooks merged. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/318. Perf run shows 18% lower shed rate versus naive global rate limit for mixed-priority traces.
2026-02-27 - UX feedback from PM (Sofia Martinez): ensure API returns structured retry-after metadata for queued requests. Added estimated_wait_ms in enqueue response payloads.
2026-03-01 - Security review kickoff: request to verify that per-tenant token usage metrics cannot be used to infer other tenants' traffic patterns. Security will audit on 2026-03-05.
